method: Claude target = multiple x next-fiscal-year consensus EPS (Yahoo Finance consensus feed, LSEG/S&P Global data). Prices: snapshot A (electrification, interconnects) = latest full-session close available on the morning of 2 Oct 2026, New York time (1 Oct 2026 for US and European listings, 2 Oct 2026 for Asian listings, 30 Sep 2026 for mainland China); snapshot B (generation, providers) = 2 Oct 2026 close for every listing (30 Sep 2026 for mainland China; 1 Oct for Saudi and Indian listings). The close_date field states the date used for each row.

electrification.theme: Extra-high-voltage transformers, built in the US

electrification.name: Infineon Technologies
electrification.theme: Power semiconductors for every stage of an 800 V hall

electrification.name: Delta Electronics
electrification.theme: Rack power, 800 V systems, battery backup, solid-state transformers

electrification.name: Lite-On Technology
electrification.theme: Number two in AI rack power and GPU power smoothing

electrification.name: Powell Industries
electrification.theme: Engineered medium-voltage switchgear and power rooms

electrification.name: onsemi
electrification.theme: Silicon carbide and power devices with operating leverage

electrification.name: Flex

electrification.name: LS Corp
electrification.theme: Korean holding company: HVDC cable, magnet wire, LS Electric

electrification.name: Vicor
electrification.theme: Vertical power delivery patents: real physics, binary outcome

electrification.name: Eaton
electrification.why: The best-placed US incumbent: an IEC-certified medium-voltage solid-state transformer, Bussmann DC fuses and Boyd liquid cooling. Americas electrical orders were +41% [P1-89].

electrification.name: ABB
electrification.why: Holds the first IEC-certified solid-state DC breaker (SACE Infinitus), a medium-voltage UPS and a stake in DG Matrix, but trades at about 27× 2027 earnings, and consensus is "hold". ABB sold its power-grids business to Hitachi in 2020–22, so it is not an HVDC supplier.

electrification.name: Vertiv
electrification.why: A real 800 V portfolio (rack and pod in 2027, hall in 2028) and leadership in liquid cooling, but a consensus favorite whose central-UPS franchise faces the 2028+ mix shift.

electrification.name: Schneider Electric
electrification.why: Triple-digit data-center growth is already in its 24× multiple, and it has no shipping 800 V switchboard or solid-state transformer yet.

electrification.name: Hitachi (Hitachi Energy)
electrification.why: The broadest owner of the scarce high-voltage stack (about 1 in 6 of the world's transformers, 1 in 4 high-voltage switchgear, more than 175 GW of HVDC links), but the stock is only about 5% below its high [P3-8].

electrification.name: Prysmian
electrification.why: The HVDC-cable oligopoly is running "flat out" with "no pricing pressure", but it is fully recognized, and the pending Atkore deal dilutes quality [P3-69].

electrification.name: Nexans
electrification.why: The value member of the cable oligopoly, at about 14.5× 2027 earnings with a €7.7 billion transmission backlog [P3-72]. It is not a top pick because its AI exposure is indirect, through grid connections.

electrification.name: Quanta Services
electrification.why: The undisputed leader in transmission construction, priced at about 34× 2027 earnings.

electrification.name: MYR Group
electrification.why: The cheapest pure electrical contractor with transmission leverage, about 41% below its high. Its transmission revenue has not yet inflected.

electrification.name: Monolithic Power Systems
electrification.why: An excellent franchise (data-center revenue +164%), but it trades at about 39× 2027 earnings and is named in two of Vicor's ITC cases [P1-42].

electrification.name: LS Electric
electrification.why: It holds the UL 1,500 V DC breaker credential, but at about 41× 2027 earnings the cheaper route is through its parent, LS Corp.

electrification.name: Navitas Semiconductor
electrification.why: Loss-making on about $10–14 million of quarterly revenue, with 800 V revenue expected from 2027. It is an option, not an investment case.

electrification.name: Wolfspeed
electrification.why: Runs a −20% gross margin on an adjusted (non-GAAP) basis [P2-23]. Management says it needs an annual revenue run-rate of about $800 million to break even at the gross-margin level [P2-25], against about $600 million at the latest quarterly rate (my estimate).

electrification.name: Samsung Electro-Mechanics
electrification.why: Capacitors for AI power are real, but the stock is up about 520% this year and fell about 11% on the Kyber-delay report alone.

electrification.name: Fluence Energy
electrification.why: Data-center batteries are an under-modelled demand spike, but Fluence has had two guidance cuts, a failed manufacturing ramp and class actions.

electrification.name: Cleveland-Cliffs
electrification.why: It is the only US maker of grain-oriented electrical steel, but electrical and stainless steel are only about 4% of its volume, so it is a steel-cycle stock, not an AI-scarcity owner [P3-37].

generation.name: INNIO Group
generation.theme: Gas engines: the workhorse of the 2026–28 onsite build

generation.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
generation.theme: The most defensive heavy-duty turbine book

generation.name: BWX Technologies
generation.theme: Naval reactors, TRISO fuel and heavy nuclear components

generation.name: Baker Hughes

generation.name: Japan Steel Works
generation.theme: One of three forges on earth for large reactor vessels

generation.name: Centrus Energy
generation.theme: The only US-owned enricher, and the HALEU gate for advanced reactors

generation.name: Cummins
generation.theme: Large gensets, gas engines and the cheapest multiple among the engine makers

generation.name: Wärtsilä
generation.theme: Medium-speed engines, rated Hold while orders hit records

generation.name: Argan
generation.theme: The only listed US contractor whose core business is building gas power plants

generation.name: Curtiss-Wright
generation.theme: Reactor coolant pumps: three to four reactors' worth a year

generation.name: Mirion Technologies
generation.theme: Radiation measurement for every restart, uprate and new plant

generation.name: Kazatomprom
generation.theme: The lowest-cost uranium producer, at about 10× earnings

generation.name: GE Vernova
generation.why: The largest turbine book (116 GW under contract, 53 GW firm, rising to "at least 125 GW" by year-end) and pricing up 10–20 points on 2026 orders [G1-1][G1-3]. But 90% of new signings are reservations, the shares trade at about 40× 2027 earnings, and 2026 earnings include a pre-tax gain of about $4 billion on Prolec [P3-18]. The bottleneck is fully priced.

generation.name: Caterpillar
generation.why: Caterpillar equipment is 33% of permitted US onsite data-center capacity, power-generation retail sales rose 72%, the backlog is $72 billion and it is tripling large-engine capacity versus 2024 [G1-16][G1-17][G1-56]. Construction and mining are still two-thirds of sales, and $2.2 billion of 2026 tariff costs weigh on margins.

generation.name: Generac
generation.why: An agreement to supply Amazon's data centers with backup generators worth up to $8 billion, of which about $2.4 billion is scheduled for 2027–28, with warrants on about 1.69 million shares that vest as Amazon buys [G1-35]. The residential business is cyclical, and the large-megawatt capacity only triples by the third quarter of 2027.

generation.name: Solaris Energy Infrastructure
generation.why: A "behind-the-meter utility": 950 MW earning, about 2.3 GW contracted and 800 MW uncontracted with near-term delivery, with $1.4 billion of liquidity [G1-25]. One customer group (xAI) dominates, the fleet's value falls when turbines become available again in 2029–30, and the Southaven permits are in litigation.

generation.name: Rolls-Royce
generation.why: mtu Series 4000 engines and the British SMR program, but Power Systems is under a quarter of the group and the shares are priced at about 30× for civil aerospace and defense [G1-33].

generation.name: ATI
generation.why: Nickel superalloys and forgings for turbine hot sections, but specialty energy is about 5% of revenue and aerospace sets the 30× multiple [G1-44].

generation.name: Carpenter Technology
generation.why: Superalloys for aerospace and energy; energy is about 5% of sales [G1-45]. A good aerospace cycle stock, not a turbine bottleneck owner.

generation.name: Fluor
generation.why: Wants gas-plant engineering and construction work, but expects meaningful awards only from the first half of 2027, and its backlog fell 4.7% [G1-50]; its NuScale stake is being monetized.

generation.name: Doosan Enerbility
generation.why: Unique assets: the world's largest nuclear forging press and the only new heavy-duty turbine entrant in a generation, with 7 of the 29 firm US large-turbine orders of the first half of 2026 and deliveries from May 2029 [G1-11][G1-10][G2-79]. At about 78× 2027 earnings, after Korean retail flows, the assets are priced; I would reconsider below 50×.

generation.name: Sprott Physical Uranium Trust
generation.why: The cleanest way to own uranium itself (81.7 million pounds in the trust) without company risk [G2-70]. The term price is already a record and the physical tightness is a 2028–35 story, so I treat it as a hold rather than a buy today.

generation.name: Bloom Energy
generation.why: The permit-light onsite option that Oracle chose (up to 2.8 GW), with about 3.8 GW booked against 0.03 GW for FuelCell Energy, the other US solid-oxide maker [G1-38][G1-54]. At about 58× 2027 earnings, above the analysts' mean target, with 73% of quarterly revenue from one customer and a disputed scandium supply chain [G1-37][G1-39], the price outweighs the position.

generation.name: Oklo
generation.why: A $6.7 billion market value on $1.2 million of trailing revenue. The Groves criticality in August 2026 is real but belongs to a 15-megawatt-thermal isotope test reactor; the 75 MW Aurora targets 2028 at best, and the "15 GW order book" is letters of intent [G2-45][G2-47][G2-49].

generation.name: NuScale Power
generation.why: The only US-approved small-modular design, but no construction-permit application, a non-binding 6 GW framework with ENTRA1 and TVA, $10.7 million of trailing revenue and a UBS Sell [G2-43].

generation.name: X-energy
generation.why: The one developer with its own fuel plant under construction, a construction-permit application through environmental review (safety review due November 2026) and two anchor customers (Dow and Amazon) [G2-53][G2-102]. It is the name to revisit after the NRC decision; today it is a $5.8 billion value on $150 million of revenue and a $449 million trailing loss.

generation.name: NANO Nuclear Energy
generation.why: An $839 million value on $214,000 of revenue, with a construction-permit review running to late 2027 [G2-50].

generation.name: Fermi America
generation.why: A Texas campus with gas turbines on site and AP1000 ambitions for 2032 and beyond, $91.7 million of cash against $520 million of debt [G2-34]: a real-estate and gas financing story.

generation.name: Babcock & Wilcox
generation.why: A real 1.2 GW boiler-and-steam-turbine contract and a backlog up from $488 million to $2.6 billion, but $240 million of debt against $57 million of equity, and a workaround that ends when turbines return [G1-47][G1-48].

generation.name: FuelCell Energy
generation.why: A 37 MW annualized production rate and falling revenue, two orders of magnitude behind Bloom [G1-40].

generation.name: Uranium Energy
generation.why: A $4.6 billion value for a small producer whose pounds the data-center thesis does not need before 2030; the term price is already a record [G2-68].

generation.name: NexGen Energy
generation.why: The development-stage name to watch (Rook I licensed for construction in March 2026), but pre-production and valued at about $6 billion; timing, not quality, is the objection [G2-90].

providers.name: Vistra
providers.theme: Hedged merchant fleet in the two tightest markets

providers.name: Constellation Energy
providers.theme: The only multi-gigawatt, already-interconnected clean supply a hyperscaler can contract before 2028

providers.name: Talen Energy
providers.theme: Fixed 2028 capacity revenue and the largest single hyperscaler nuclear contract

providers.name: PPL Corporation
providers.theme: Wires in the PJM zones that carry the growth, with 11 GW signed

providers.name: Sempra
providers.theme: Oncor: the Texas grid connection, which is the scarce good

providers.name: Public Service Enterprise Group
providers.theme: A wires valuation with an unhedged nuclear option in PJM

providers.name: Kinder Morgan
providers.theme: The pipe into the Southeast, where no new gas arrives before 2028

providers.name: Kodiak Gas Services
providers.theme: Compression horsepower and a 1 GW turbine allocation: the quiet onsite-power beneficiary

providers.name: EQT
providers.theme: Appalachian gas next to PJM's load, with its own pipes

providers.name: NRG Energy
providers.theme: The first disclosed "paid for megawatts, not utilization" gas contract

providers.name: FirstEnergy
providers.theme: The fastest-growing contracted book relative to system size among wires utilities

providers.name: Energy Transfer
providers.theme: Texas intrastate pipe: no federal certificate needed

providers.name: Capital Power
providers.theme: Alberta's surplus gas capacity, contracted to Meta from 2028

providers.name: Williams
providers.why: The AI gas utility: Transco's Southeast expansion (1.6 Bcf/d, Q4 2027), a 2.6 GW behind-the-meter power portfolio funded by Blackstone at a 6.35% equity cost cap, a "6 GW+" power backlog and an 11%-plus growth target [U2-5][U2-48][U2-19]. The highest quality in midstream, at the highest multiple (about 27× 2027).

providers.name: Xcel Energy
providers.why: Long-term growth raised to 9%-plus on a $70 billion plan with 85% of equity pre-funded, a "high probability" portfolio of more than 20 GW and a Plains and Texas footprint in the load-shift corridor [U1-63]. About 16× 2027 with a 3.3% yield; wildfire liability in Colorado and Texas is the risk.

providers.name: NextEra Energy
providers.why: A 35.1 GW renewables and storage backlog, 30–40 data-center hubs in discussion, 9.5 GW of gas in development, the Duane Arnold restart for Google by 2029 and the pending Dominion merger [U2-21][U1-53][U1-54]. Good assets at one of the highest regulated multiples; the Virginia merger conditions are the swing factor.

providers.name: Southern Company
providers.why: Contracted load of 17 GW (+6 GW in a quarter), the 3.2 GW OpenAI contract with 1 GW of flexibility and about 10 GW of approved new generation [U1-56][U1-57]. Georgia bills rose $43 a month in two years, the commission faces elections, and the Hold consensus reflects that tension [U1-58].

providers.name: Duke Energy
providers.why: A $103 billion plan, 7.8 GW of executed data-center agreements and large combined-cycle builds, but $10 billion of equity to issue in 2027–30 and a 9.8% allowed return [U1-62]. Fair rather than cheap.

providers.name: American Electric Power
providers.why: 63 GW "contracted", 90% data centers, and the template large-load tariff in Ohio, but that tariff cut AEP Ohio's working queue from more than 30 GW to 13 GW, and a $78 billion plan makes equity the swing factor [U1-14][U1-13].

providers.name: Entergy
providers.why: The Meta Hyperion package: $15 billion of capital, seven combined-cycle plants and a capital plan raised 30% to $57 billion [U1-59]. Single-customer concentration at the highest multiple in the regulated set.

providers.name: Dominion Energy
providers.why: 12 GW of firm data-center agreements in Northern Virginia and the pending merger with NextEra at 0.8138 shares; the allowed return was cut to 9.8% and upgrades are now assigned directly to data centers [U1-52][U1-16][U1-18]. The merger spread is too thin to be the reason to own it.

providers.name: CenterPoint Energy
providers.why: Houston wires serving about 14 GW of eligible load by 2031 and a regulator-friendly story of at least $5 billion of delivery-charge reductions [U1-67]. The purest Texas connection play, at the richest multiple in the wires set (about 18× 2027).

providers.name: DT Midstream
providers.why: A $3.4 billion backlog and 7.5 Bcf/d of potential Midwest demand from 50 GW of announced large loads [U2-10], but about 25× 2027 earnings for mid-single-digit growth.

providers.name: Enbridge
providers.why: The only company here that sells both the gas and the solar-plus-storage to the same hyperscaler (Meta), inside a C$41 billion secured backlog, with a 6% yield [U2-38][U2-81]. Leverage of 5.1× and a rate-driven de-rating; consensus earnings are in Canadian dollars and were converted for the New York line.

providers.name: TC Energy
providers.why: Two Columbia expansions explicitly for data-center generation (0.7 Bcf/d, 2028–30) in a $20 billion-plus project pipeline [U2-8][U2-83]. A close call; the leverage target of 4.75× tips it to Hold.

providers.name: Archrock
providers.why: Compression at 94% utilization with a 665,000-horsepower ten-year contract, but Caterpillar lead times of 195–200 weeks cap its growth, and Kodiak has the turbine allocation [U2-11]. Cheaper than Kodiak at about 14× 2027.

providers.name: RWE
providers.why: The exception in Europe: 30 connected sites suitable for data centers, two deals "nearing agreement", 10 GW of US capacity secured and Germany's gas-plant tenders [U2-30][U2-41]. About 18× 2027 earnings near its high; the European power-contract market collapsed around it.

providers.name: Expand Energy
providers.why: The largest US gas producer, with the Haynesville volume behind every Southeast pipeline project, at about 10× 2027 earnings and 30% below its high. Management says liquefied natural gas, not data centers, leads demand [U2-56]: a gas-price trade with a data-center option.

providers.name: Exelon
providers.why: The cheapest wires name (about 13× 2027, 4.1% yield), but its high-probability load fell 40% once collateral was required, it withdrew a Pennsylvania rate request, and it is the most exposed to Pennsylvania and Illinois affordability politics [U1-19][U1-35]. I would reconsider below 12×.

providers.name: Edison International
providers.why: Wildfire liability and no disclosed data-center pipeline; a yield above 6% is a warning, not an invitation.

providers.name: AES
providers.why: A $15-per-share cash take-private by GIP and EQT approved by shareholders, closing late 2026 or early 2027; the spread is under 1% [U1-73][U2-22]. A merger-arbitrage position, not a thesis.

providers.name: Ormat Technologies
providers.why: The only non-nuclear firm, carbon-free resource a hyperscaler can contract today: 150 MW of geothermal for Google through Nevada's Clean Transition Tariff (2028–30) and a Switch contract [U2-24]. At about 36× 2027 earnings after a 36% fall, I would wait for the Nevada regulator's decision and a lower price.

providers.name: Clearway Energy
providers.why: Contracted renewables with no verified data-center contract, at about 18× 2027 earnings.

providers.name: Comstock Resources
providers.why: Host of NextEra's proposed 5.2 GW, $16 billion Western Haynesville power hub, which could take almost 1 Bcf/d by 2031 [U2-15]. The hub is 2029–31, the stock is 53% below its high on depressed earnings, and the thesis is gas price first.

providers.name: Iberdrola
providers.why: Land, grid and a €2 billion Spanish data-center joint venture (headlines) [U2-90][U2-92], but a Hold consensus with about 1% upside and a European power-contract market that collapsed [U2-31].

providers.name: Korea Electric Power
providers.why: A policy instrument with ₩202 trillion of debt, eleven new regional price zones and a request that chipmakers prepay $18 billion of power bills [U2-34][U2-70]. Down 56% from its high; the data-center load is a cost it must serve, not a profit.

providers.name: Tokyo Electric Power
providers.why: A reported data center near its Kashiwazaki nuclear plant moved the shares in December 2025 [U2-73], but pass-through tariffs and the Fukushima liabilities limit the upside; 44% below its high.

providers.name: ACWA Power
providers.why: Gulf AI power (Stargate UAE, Saudi Humain) is real but state-directed; returns are set by the state, the consensus is "underperform", and the shares are 34% below their high.

interconnects.name: Mitsui Kinzoku (Mitsui Mining & Smelting)

interconnects.name: Sumitomo Electric Industries
interconnects.theme: InP substrates, lasers, optical connectors and fiber

interconnects.name: Coherent
interconnects.theme: 6-inch InP lasers, light sources for co-packaged optics, transceivers

interconnects.name: TSMC
interconnects.theme: COUPE co-packaged optics, SoIC 3D stacking, CoWoS

interconnects.name: JX Advanced Metals
interconnects.theme: InP substrates and semiconductor sputtering targets

interconnects.name: BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi)
interconnects.theme: Hybrid bonding and photonics die attach

interconnects.name: Nittobo (Nitto Boseki)
interconnects.theme: Low-expansion T-glass and low-loss glass cloth

interconnects.name: Credo Technology
interconnects.theme: Active electrical cables, retimers and optical signal processors

interconnects.name: Lumentum
interconnects.why: The highest-quality InP franchise: one of two 200G modulated-laser suppliers with Broadcom, ultra-high-power lasers for co-packaged optics, and pump lasers sold out. It trades within 1% of its high at about 48× fiscal 2027 and 30× fiscal 2028 earnings.

interconnects.name: Ciena
interconnects.why: Coherent optics and line systems for data-center interconnect. Fiscal Q3 revenue rose 37% and fiscal 2026 guidance is $6.42 billion, but two customers are 41.7% of revenue [X-1].

interconnects.name: Corning
interconnects.why: Fiber and connectivity: optical sales +32% and enterprise +65% on generative-AI products in Q2 2026, with its Springboard targets (raised in May) reaffirmed [X-2]. It trades at about 37× 2027 earnings.

interconnects.name: Fujikura
interconnects.why: High-density fiber and cable for AI data centers; already re-rated.

interconnects.name: Marvell
interconnects.why: Owns Celestial AI's Photonic Fabric (optical scale-up and optics into memory) plus optical signal processors and custom silicon, at about 40× fiscal 2028 earnings. Investor Day is on 6 October.

interconnects.name: Arista Networks
interconnects.why: The scale-out Ethernet leader, near its high at about 39× 2027 earnings.

interconnects.name: Amphenol
interconnects.why: A connector franchise that does not depend on the medium (copper, fiber and power). Rubin's cable-less tray removed some exclusive content.

interconnects.name: Tower Semiconductor
interconnects.why: The merchant silicon-photonics foundry leader (run-rate $680 million, heading above $1 billion in Q4 2026), but at about 36× 2027 earnings, and four 300 mm silicon-photonics expansions converge in 2027–29 [I2-58].

interconnects.name: Soitec
interconnects.why: Reportedly about 95% of 300 mm photonics silicon-on-insulator wafers (a secondary estimate) [I2-61], with that revenue growing 2.5–3× in fiscal 2027 [I2-62]. The stock is up about 580% this year, and consensus sits at about the current price.

interconnects.name: Elite Material
interconnects.why: The number one high-speed laminate maker (about 39% share) [I3-62]. It is up 215% this year and squeezed between foil and glass suppliers that have pricing power.

interconnects.name: Fabrinet
interconnects.why: About 40% below its high after NVIDIA fell to 16% of fiscal 2026 revenue [X-3]. Co-packaged optics moves optical-engine assembly toward TSMC and Foxconn, but Fabrinet is a non-Chinese manufacturing route if US rules tighten.

interconnects.name: Celestica
interconnects.why: Switch and rack integration at about 19× 2027 earnings; named in Vicor's September 2026 patent complaint at the US International Trade Commission.

interconnects.name: InnoLight (Zhongji Innolight)
interconnects.why: The world's largest 800G / 1.6T transceiver maker (first-half 2026 net profit CN¥13.65 billion) at only about 12× 2027 earnings. It is cheap for a reason: it was added to the Pentagon's 1260H list on 8 June 2026, and a Treasury listing would bar US persons from holding it [X-4][X-5]. Figures use the Shenzhen line (15 analysts); the Hong Kong line (HK$1,072 on 2 October) has only three analyst targets.

interconnects.name: Astera Labs
interconnects.why: Excellent scale-up position, but about 56× 2027 earnings and 20× 2027 sales, already past the bull case.

interconnects.name: AXT
interconnects.why: InP substrate leverage, but all crystal growth is in China, US-customer export permits are pending, and the stock trades at about 36× 2027 earnings [I2-21].

interconnects.name: POET Technologies
interconnects.why: An optical-interposer story valued at $1.3 billion on about $1.7 million of trailing revenue; its Marvell partnership ended.

interconnects.name: Lightwave Logic
interconnects.why: Electro-optic polymers valued at $0.8 billion on about $0.25 million of trailing revenue; long-term polymer reliability is unproven.

interconnects.name: SKC (Absolics glass core)
interconnects.why: Glass-core substrate mass production pushed to 2027; loss-making [I3-70].

interconnects.name: Applied Optoelectronics
interconnects.why: A transceiver maker that lost about $57 million over the last twelve months [I2-78]. Consensus expects a turn to profit in 2027, and after a 208% rise this year the shares already trade at about 23× those 2027 earnings.
